cue: How do I like architecture to be done?
the_answer: Tom wants architecture decided BEFORE writing code: the first question is always 'where does this live architecturally?' (which file, which class, which layer). Each area should have its own responsibility — good architecture makes you MORE efficient, not less, because changes stay local (Rule D). The default move is to EXTEND existing code, not create new functions/files (fragmentation compounds; reuse structures 'we will never find'). Keep it simple and robust, surgical and clean — 'assume an expert engineer will review it: simple, clean, everything in the right place.' Tom does not read the code, so the assistant is the sole architectural guardian.

essential.why: The WHY behind 894795e3. Locked. Each area owns its responsibility (DAL for SQL, brain methods for logic, hooks for dispatch) so changes are LOCAL. essential.title: Extend before creating — architectural fragmentation is more expensive than one more parameter
essential.why: The operative default of how Tom wants code done: extend an existing function/centralize before spawning a new one; new files are structural commitments needing justification. Counter-rule included (don't extend past coherence — split when a function does six things). Locked seed principle. silver.why: The quality bar Tom applies: 'assume an expert engineer will review it, simple, clean and everything in the right place.' Every function in the file whose purpose matches it, no duplicated mechanisms, no dead code, names that make ownership obvious. Verbatim Tom quote.

silver.title: Architecture principle: clean architecture means reusing existing structures, not remaking what you can't find
silver.why: Tom verbatim: 'every component should do its own thing, let's reuse existing functions, structures not remake stuff that we will never find.' Findability framing of the extend-before-creating preference. Supports 894795e3.

silver.title: DAL-first rule: reuse existing DAL functions, never write dedicated query functions outside DAL
silver.why: Concrete instance of the responsibility/extend preference: DB access lives in the DAL layer; extend a DAL method or add one, never inline queries in feature code. Tom verbatim. A specific application, hence silver.

silver.title: Senior-engineer discipline: read before implementing, extend before creating
silver.why: Tom verbatim: 'Act like a senior engineer not an intern' — READ code before implementing, reuse/unite/extend. Process-side of the architecture preference (investigate first), strong supporting node.

silver.title: Simple and robust: Tom's governing directive for brain architecture
silver.why: Tom verbatim: 'Clean code, smart architecture, we need it to be simple and robust.' The simplicity-first axis — stabilize before adding architecture, simplify the hot path, fewer rules over clever-complete. Directly relevant nuance.

silver.why: How Tom wants big architectural changes approached: trace and present the call stack (who calls this, what it calls, what depends on it) BEFORE touching anything. The 'trace before changing' procedural preference.

silver.why: The accountability context: Tom judges by outcomes, not by reading code, so the assistant is the sole architectural guardian. Explains WHY these self-imposed rules exist. Tom verbatim quote. Frames the whole preference but doesn't state it.
